sources.name: Leonida Legend dispute desk
sources.detail: This guide's cross-check of S1 against S2 wording; where the two agree, the dispute is settled.

disputes.topic: Does the platinum need the online-style partner trophies?
disputes.claim: One camp says Hot Together and Retail Therapy need a second player online; the other says the in-game partner counts.
disputes.resolution: Settled by the wording both lists share: each description says "with your partner", and the product page sells a two-protagonist partner system, not an online mode [S30]. The partner is Jason or Lucia as the AI companion, so both trophies are single-player work [S45].

disputes.topic: Is "A Long Road" 100% the same as every other trophy?
disputes.claim: Some hunters assume 100% completion automatically grants every collectible trophy on the way.
disputes.resolution: Not so: the list gives collectibles their own trophies with their own counts (250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots, 3 card sets), and PSN tracks those counts separately from the 100% statistic [S2]. Treat 100% as its own checklist and the counted trophies as parallel work [S19].

disputes.topic: Which trophies are hidden — 27 or 28?
disputes.claim: Early list posts disagreed on the hidden count.
disputes.resolution: Both frozen sources agree on 28 hidden of 55, and this guide flags exactly those 28 [S1][S20]. The story spine (ids 2–13) accounts for twelve of them [S48].

disputes.topic: Is "Catch Me If You Can" missable?
disputes.claim: Forum posts split: some say the VCIA departure can be repeated any time, others warn it is a one-time story beat.
disputes.resolution: The description's wording — "an unscheduled departure" — describes a specific story moment at VCIA, not a repeatable free-roam action, and the trophy sits hidden, the usual mark of a story beat [S1][S9]. This guide flags it missable: take the unscheduled way out during the VCIA story visit, before the mission resolves [S19].

disputes.topic: Can "In The Beginning…" be earned after the story?
disputes.claim: Because Ocean Beach is open world, some assume the cocktail moment waits forever.
disputes.resolution: The description ties the moment to a view on Ocean Beach in the game's opening framing — the title itself is "In The Beginning…" — so this guide treats the first Ocean Beach visit as the window and flags it missable [S1][S43]. Have the cocktail early; it costs two minutes [S19].

disputes.topic: Does "Personal Best" need a specific ending?
disputes.claim: The vague description ("A partnership with mass appeal") led to claims it depends on an ending choice.
disputes.resolution: Nothing in either list ties it to an ending; both describe a partnership moment, and the trophy is hidden like the other story beats [S1][S2]. This guide flags it missable on the story path and places it in Chapter 2–3, where partnership beats concentrate [S19].

disputes.topic: How many choices does "Actions Speak Louder" track?
disputes.claim: Guesses ranged from a handful of big choices to every dialogue pick.
disputes.resolution: PSN's own progress target settles it: the count runs to 500, so ordinary play makes most of them and only the story-locked ones can be missed [S2]. Flagged missable because a skipped branch cannot be re-chosen on the same save [S21].

disputes.topic: Is "Bad Luck, I Guess" a fail-state trophy?
disputes.claim: Some read "Second time's the charm" as failing a mission once; others as retrying any activity.
disputes.resolution: Both lists leave it deliberately vague and hidden [S1]. The safe reading used here: it belongs to a story sequence where the first attempt is scripted to fall short, so it is flagged missable and earned on the story path, not farmed in free roam [S19][S22].

disputes.topic: "The Truth Is Out There" — random event or story beat?
disputes.claim: The description ("What the hell just happened?") gives nothing away, and posts argue both ways.
disputes.resolution: It is hidden and sits among the stranger-strand trophies in the list's own ordering, so this guide routes it through the stranger content and flags it missable rather than leaving it to random encounters [S1][S28].

disputes.topic: Do stunt counts carry between Lucia and Jason?
disputes.claim: Hunters asked whether the 250 stunts must be done as one character.
disputes.resolution: PSN tracks one count per trophy, not per character, and the forum ruling agrees: the 250 is a single shared counter [S2][S21]. Split the stunt route between both protagonists freely [S25].

disputes.topic: Are there 9 activity types or more?
disputes.claim: The starter hint says 9; some lists of activities run longer.
disputes.resolution: The official guide line in both frozen sources says each type once, and the activity index this guide follows names nine types [S1][S27]. Extra variants (a second race class, say) are flavours of a type, not new types [S48].

disputes.topic: Shooting Range: 42 challenges, gold in all?
disputes.claim: A silver for "a gold medal in all" seemed steep, and some hoped silvers counted.
disputes.resolution: The description is unambiguous — gold in all — and PSN's target is 42 [S1][S2]. Budget real practice time; it is the longest silver on the list [S39].

disputes.topic: Top Fun: win at every location, or just enter?
disputes.claim: Some read "Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location" as participation.
disputes.resolution: The verb is "win" and the target is 14 locations [S1][S2]. A podium does not count; the tracker counter in this guide only advances on a win [S37].

disputes.topic: "Win 20 different races" — repeats allowed?
disputes.claim: Can you win the same race 20 times?
disputes.resolution: No: the description says 20 different races, so the counter tracks distinct events [S1]. This guide's steps spread the wins across race classes to double-count progress toward Master of None [S27].

disputes.topic: Is Cal's fishing challenge story-locked?
disputes.claim: Posts disagreed on whether Cal appears only inside a mission.
disputes.resolution: Cal is one of the named contacts in the strangers index, and his challenge is repeatable from his spot once introduced [S28]. Not flagged missable; the risk is only putting it off [S38].

disputes.topic: Stranger finals: do they expire?
disputes.claim: Five trophies each ask for a contact's final mission; players feared strands expire as chapters pass.
disputes.resolution: Neither list marks any stranger trophy hidden-by-chapter or missable, and the strands index treats the finals as persistent map content [S1][S28]. This guide still schedules them before the finale out of caution, and says so [S19].

disputes.topic: How many stranger strands does silver need — 8 exactly?
disputes.claim: Some read "8 mission strands" as eight specific strands.
disputes.resolution: The description counts any 8 strands across Leonida, and the five named-contact finals are five of them [S1][S28]. Finish the named five first, then the three shortest remaining strands [S19].

disputes.topic: Meditation spots: 18, and do they need daylight?
disputes.claim: A rumour said some spots only work at sunrise.
disputes.resolution: The count is 18 in both sources and neither adds a time condition [S1][S2]. This guide routes them in one sweep and notes the rumour as unproven rather than a step [S40][S48].

disputes.topic: Card sets: any 3, or 3 specific sets?
disputes.claim: "Complete 3 Collectible Card sets" left open whether the sets are chosen for you.
disputes.resolution: The description names no set, so any three complete sets satisfy it; PSN's target is 3 [S1][S2]. This guide picks the three sets whose cards cluster on the story route [S25].

disputes.topic: WAiNK spots: do repeats at one spot count?
disputes.claim: The verb phrase "WAiNK It at 100 locations" was read as 100 uses anywhere.
disputes.resolution: "Locations" is the operative word and the target is 100, so each spot counts once [S1][S2]. The tracker treats WAiNK spots like other collectibles [S23].

disputes.topic: "Complete 50 Challenges" — which challenges?
disputes.claim: Some counted missions as challenges; others only the challenge board.
disputes.resolution: The description capitalises nothing and names no board; the working reading here is the game's own challenge list, tracked to 50 by PSN [S2][S42]. Story missions have their own trophies and are not double-counted in this guide's route [S19].

disputes.topic: Retail Therapy: must the wanted level survive all three shops?
disputes.claim: The wording "without losing your Wanted Level" was read two ways: never drop a star, or never fully clear it.
disputes.resolution: The natural reading of both lists is that the wanted level must never be lost (fully cleared or busted) across the three robberies [S1][S48]. Plan an escape route that keeps heat on between shops [S34].

disputes.topic: Discover 100 vehicles: sit in them, or see them?
disputes.claim: "Discover" was argued both ways.
disputes.resolution: The vehicle index counts a vehicle as discovered when it is entered and registered by the game, the same verb the Scooter Bros trophy uses for its 10 [S26][S36]. This guide's steps say: get in, don't just photograph it [S19].

disputes.topic: Combat Focus takedowns: kills or knockdowns?
disputes.claim: "Take down 5 enemies in a single use" — some insisted kills only.
disputes.resolution: The description says take down, and the systems coverage describes Combat Focus as a slow-motion takedown window [S1][S13]. Count knockdowns; line up five targets before triggering it [S19].

disputes.topic: "Challenging Tank" — steal a Rhino or survive one?
disputes.claim: The jokey description ("Kinda hot in these Rhinos") split readers.
disputes.resolution: "In these Rhinos" puts you inside one, so this guide's steps are about getting into a Rhino and using it, not fighting one [S1][S48]. It is a free-roam trophy: earn it whenever a Rhino can be taken [S22].

disputes.topic: Bank vaults: 5 different vaults?
disputes.claim: Some planned to rob the same vault five times.
disputes.resolution: The description counts vaults robbed and escaped, and the guide coverage treats each bank as a distinct job [S1][S41]. This guide routes five different banks and says so in the steps [S19].

disputes.topic: Explore all of Leonida: 52 areas — enter or reveal?
disputes.claim: Map-completion arguments: driving through a corner vs fully revealing each area.
disputes.resolution: PSN's target is 52 areas and the map threads treat an area as explored when its name registers on entry [S2][S18]. Cross each area's heartland, not just its border road [S19].

disputes.topic: Pest Control: one operation per gang — all 9 gangs?
disputes.claim: Some thought any nine operations would do.
disputes.resolution: The description says "belonging to each gang", and the reporting names nine Leonida gangs, so it is one operation for each of the nine [S1][S33]. The tracker lists them by gang, not by count alone [S19].

disputes.topic: Showroom smash: any showroom, any vehicle?
disputes.claim: "In classic style" was read as needing a specific car.
disputes.resolution: Neither list names a car or a showroom; the requirement is the act — drive out through the glass [S1][S43]. Any vehicle showroom on the map qualifies in this guide's reading [S22].

disputes.topic: Bowling trophies: two trophies, one alley?
disputes.claim: Players conflated Let's Go Bowling with Ten Pin.
disputes.resolution: They are separate: one is the follow-through game at the Kolt & Associates alley, the other a melee drive-by knockdown anywhere [S1]. The alley visit earns the first; the second is a free-roam stunt [S19].

disputes.topic: Laundering: does story income count toward $250,000?
disputes.claim: Some banked story payouts toward Dime on the Dollar.
disputes.resolution: The description specifies laundering Marked Bills through contacts — a specific activity, not general income — and PSN tracks $250,000 of it [S1][S2]. Only marked-bill runs advance this guide's counter [S42].

disputes.topic: Spend $100,000: properties included?
disputes.claim: "Across all shops" — garages are bought, not shopped, said one camp.
disputes.resolution: The description says shops, and garages carry their own trophy (Little Boxes), so this guide counts shop spending only and keeps the two budgets separate [S1][S35].

disputes.topic: Garages: 8 properties — all purchasable from the start?
disputes.claim: Some listings implied late-game locks on some garages.
disputes.resolution: Neither source adds a lock; the target is 8 [S1][S2]. This guide still schedules purchases late, when cash is plentiful, and flags the assumption openly [S19][S48].

disputes.topic: Scooter Bros: register vehicles you own, or any 10?
disputes.claim: "Register 10 vehicles to the app" — ownership unclear.
disputes.resolution: The coverage describes registration as an app action on vehicles you drive, owned or not [S36]. This guide's steps register daily drivers as you discover them, finishing alongside Whip It Good [S19].

disputes.topic: Chapter trophies: one per chapter, plus prologue and finale?
disputes.claim: The spine looked uneven: an opening-mission trophy, chapter trophies, then a gold finale.
disputes.resolution: The list is exactly that: Gone Fishing has its own trophy, Chapters 1–4 have theirs, and the final mission is the gold [S1][S6]. The roadmap's first three stages follow this spine one-to-one [S19].

disputes.topic: Is there an online trophy hidden in the list?
disputes.claim: The task brief allows an online kind, and some expected at least one online trophy.
disputes.resolution: No description in either frozen source mentions online play, an online mode or other players [S1][S2]. Every trophy on the list is earnable in the single-player game as described, so this guide uses no online kind [S48].

roadmap.title: Arrival in Leonida
roadmap.summary: Play the opening and Chapter 1, take the Ocean Beach cocktail while the beginning is still the beginning, and sample the activity types as they unlock.
roadmap.notes: Two of this stage's trophies are time-sensitive: In The Beginning… belongs to the opening hours [S1], and Master of None is cheapest while every new activity is still a first [S27].

roadmap.title: Chapters 2–3: Vice City Opens Up
roadmap.summary: Push the story through Chapters 2 and 3, clearing Breakfast Run and The Cartel Heist, and take the unscheduled way out of VCIA when the story puts you there.
roadmap.notes: Catch Me If You Can and Personal Best are both flagged missable in this window: the VCIA visit and the partnership beat do not repeat on a finished save [S9][S19].

roadmap.title: Chapters 4–Finale: The Long Road Home
roadmap.summary: Finish the story spine: Chapter 4, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown, Operation Savage Glory and the final mission, making your choices count as you go.
roadmap.notes: Actions Speak Louder tracks choices to 500 and Bad Luck, I Guess hides in a scripted second attempt — both are earned on this path or not at all [S2][S22].

roadmap.title: Strangers, Freaks & Side Hustles
roadmap.summary: Run the stranger strands to their finals — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — hunt Bret's unique animal, and keep an eye out for the strange thing.
roadmap.notes: Eight finished strands earn the silver; the five named finals are five of them, so only three more strands are needed [S1][S28].

roadmap.title: Completionist Sweep: Collectibles & the Map
roadmap.summary: One long sweep of Leonida: meditation spots, card sets, WAiNK spots, vehicle discoveries, all 52 areas, the garages and the Scooter Bros registrations.
roadmap.notes: Route the sweep region by region so the 52-area exploration and the counted collectibles advance together [S18][S25].

roadmap.title: Grinds: Activities, Crime & Cash
roadmap.summary: The counted grinds: 250 stunts, 42 range golds, drone races, challenges, robberies, gang operations, laundering and spending.
roadmap.notes: This is the longest stage. The Shooting Range golds and the stunt count reward short daily sessions over one marathon [S16][S39].

roadmap.title: The Long Road: 100% & the Platinum
roadmap.summary: Close out the 100% checklist — whatever strands, counts and one-offs remain — and the platinum lands with the last of the 54.
roadmap.notes: Keep a reserve list from stage 1: anything skipped earlier lands here, so sweep stages 4–6 clean before you start [S19].

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the list itself: PlayStation awards it when the other 54 trophies are earned, and both frozen sources describe it in exactly those terms [S1][S2]. There is no shortcut and no separate task — your real guide is the roadmap in this app: seven stages that order the 54 so the missables are taken in their windows and the counted grinds run in parallel [S19]. If one trophy is holding the platinum, it is almost always a counted one (250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots) rather than a story one, so start the counters in stage 1, not stage 7 [S16].
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies; the platinum has no task of its own [S1][S2]
Follow the seven-stage roadmap so the six missables fall inside their story windows [S19]
Start every counted trophy (stunts, spots, vehicles, dollars) in the first stage, not the last [S16]
Keep the tracker's counters honest: advance a counter only when the game registers the act [S2]
Use the Next Up view to clear the cheapest remaining trophies first when the list thins out [S19]
When 54 are earned, the platinum unlocks on the spot — no turn-in, no menu [S3]

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission, Gone Fishing, carries its own trophy ahead of the Chapter 1 trophy, and both lists order it first among the story beats [S1][S6]. Play it straight through: it teaches the partner switch and the basics of Leonida, and nothing in it can be failed permanently [S31]. It is hidden on PlayStation, so do not be surprised when it pops without warning [S20].
steps: Start a new game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from the first scene [S6]
Follow the mission's prompts to learn the partner switch between Lucia and Jason [S30]
Finish the mission's final beat; the trophy pops as the chapter card fades [S1]
Do not skip the opening cutscenes on a first run — later stranger introductions build on them [S28]
Note the places the opening shows you — the Newswire's Leonida tour starts from this same coastline [S4]
Check the tracker after the pop: this is the first of the 28 hidden trophies, so it will not have shown in the list before now [S20]

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 closes out the game's first act, and its trophy is a pure story beat: finish the chapter and it is yours [S1]. Use the chapter to learn the map's southern coast — several stage-5 collectibles sit on ground you cross here, and noting them early shortens the later sweep [S18]. Before the chapter ends, take the Ocean Beach cocktail for In The Beginning… while the opening framing still holds [S43].
steps: Complete every Chapter 1 mission in order from the mission marker [S6]
Have the Ocean Beach cocktail with a view before the chapter closes (In The Beginning…) [S43]
Try each new activity type the chapter unlocks, once each, for Master of None [S27]
Finish the chapter finale; the trophy pops with the Chapter 2 card [S1]
Bank any new vehicle you drove this chapter — enter it, do not just pass it (Whip It Good) [S26]
Read the chapter's places against the official site's Leonida names so the stage-5 sweep map is already familiar [S29]

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: The Chapter 2 trophy carries the list's asterisked name exactly as PlayStation publishes it [S3]. The chapter widens the map and the partnership beats that Personal Best hides among, so play story-first in this window and keep a save at the chapter start [S9]. Nothing else in the chapter is missable; the two flagged trophies of this stage are the VCIA departure and the partnership moment [S19].
steps: Complete every Chapter 2 mission in order [S6]
Keep a manual save at the chapter's start — this window holds a missable partnership beat [S9]
Watch for the partnership moment the hidden trophy Personal Best describes [S1]
Finish the chapter finale; the trophy pops with the Chapter 3 card [S1]
Compare your route through the chapter with the roadmap order in the guide hub — drift is fine, missed markers are not [S10]
Top up the choice counter habit now: Chapter 3's scenes are dense with prompted choices [S2]

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter 3 is the Vice City chapter, and its trophy is another straight story beat [S1]. The VCIA story visit falls in this stretch of the game, which is why Catch Me If You Can is staged here: when the story puts you inside VCIA, take the unscheduled way out before the mission resolves [S33]. Clear Breakfast Run and The Cartel Heist in the same window; both carry their own trophies [S6].
steps: Complete every Chapter 3 mission in order [S6]
During the VCIA story visit, leave by an unscheduled departure before the mission ends (Catch Me If You Can) [S33]
Complete Breakfast Run (Trust) and The Cartel Heist (Break the Bank) as they appear [S6]
Finish the chapter finale; the trophy pops with the Chapter 4 card [S1]
Sweep any VCIA-area collectibles before leaving the airport district — returning later costs a dedicated trip [S24]
Note which gangs the chapter put you against; Pest Control needs one operation from each of the nine [S14]

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last numbered chapter before the endgame missions, and its trophy follows the same pattern as the earlier chapters [S1]. The remaining named missions — Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown and Operation Savage Glory — each carry a trophy, so sweep the mission markers as they appear rather than saving them [S6]. Your choice count for Actions Speak Louder should be climbing through this chapter; make every prompted choice rather than letting scenes time out [S2].
steps: Complete every Chapter 4 mission in order [S6]
Make every prompted story choice instead of letting it lapse (Actions Speak Louder counts to 500) [S2]
Clear Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown and Operation Savage Glory as they unlock [S6]
Finish the chapter finale to open the final mission [S1]
Before the finale, finish any stage-2 or stage-3 stragglers — the endgame window is the last easy pass at them [S19]
Check rarity context if you are chasing order: player statistics show the chapter trophies are the list's most-earned, so nothing here should be left behind [S46]

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The final mission is one of only two golds on the list, and it is a straight completion trophy: finish the mission and the gold is yours [S1][S47]. Keep a save before you start it — the endgame is where the scripted second attempt behind Bad Luck, I Guess sits, and a clean run through the finale keeps both trophies on the same pass [S22]. After the credits, the game returns you to Leonida for the long completion stages [S12].
steps: Save manually before starting the final mission [S22]
Play the finale through its scripted shortfall and second attempt without reloading (Bad Luck, I Guess) [S22]
Complete the final mission; the gold pops at the mission-complete card [S1]
After the credits, return to free roam — stages 4 to 7 all happen post-story if you prefer [S12]
Save again after the credits roll; the post-story save is the base every later stage builds on [S19]
If performance dips in the finale's biggest scenes, the technical coverage suggests the standard performance mode for a steadier run [S32]

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission with its own trophy, sitting in the Chapter 2–3 stretch of the spine [S1][S6]. It is a short, early mission: take it when its marker appears and it needs no preparation beyond a serviceable vehicle [S17]. Like the other named-mission trophies it is hidden, so it will not show in the list until it pops [S20].
steps: Pick up the Breakfast Run marker when it appears in the Chapter 2–3 window [S6]
Run the mission's errand route without swapping vehicles mid-mission [S17]
Complete the mission; the trophy pops at the completion card [S1]
Use the run to learn the errand timing — Breakfast Run is the template for Randy's delivery strand later [S28]
If a choice prompt appears on the route, take it: every choice feeds the 500-count trophy [S2]

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is the story's named heist mission and carries its own completion trophy [S1][S33]. Treat it as the template for the free-roam robberies later: the vault routine here is the same shape as the five bank vaults of Maximum Withdrawal, so learn the escape timing on this scripted version [S41]. Any approach the mission offers completes the trophy; the choice is flavour, not a fork [S6].
steps: Start The Cartel Heist from its story marker in the Chapter 2–3 window [S6]
Work the heist's stages in order and keep the crew alive through the vault [S33]
Escape the wanted level to close the mission; the trophy pops on completion [S1]
Note the vault-and-escape rhythm — it is the template for Maximum Withdrawal's five banks [S41]
Compare the heist's staging with the roadmap's heist order before you improvise your own bank routes [S8]
Bank the payout rather than spending it — the two money trophies both reward patience [S42]

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named mission in the Chapter 4 stretch, with the same hidden completion pattern as the other named missions [S1][S6]. Take it as soon as its marker appears: its area of the map also holds two of the meditation spots, and combining the trips saves a stage-5 detour [S40]. No choice inside the mission affects any other trophy [S48].
steps: Pick up the Child's Play marker in the Chapter 4 window [S6]
Complete the mission's beats in order [S17]
Detour to the two meditation spots near the mission area before you leave (Positive Mental Attitude) [S40]
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the completion card [S1]
Mark the mission area's collectibles on the same pass — the collectible maps cluster several near this district [S24]
If a strand marker is live nearby, take it now: stage 4 is shorter for every strand started early [S28]

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named Chapter 4-window mission with its own hidden trophy [S1][S6]. It plays around Vice City's nightlife and media strip, which is also where several WAiNK spots cluster — sweep them on the same trip to feed the 100-spot counter [S23]. The mission itself is a straight completion; no approach is missable [S48].
steps: Pick up the Headliners marker in the Chapter 4 window [S6]
Complete the mission's beats in order [S17]
Sweep the WAiNK spots around the nightlife strip on the same trip (You WAiNKer!) [S23]
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the completion card [S1]
The strip is also race country — a first race win here starts Earn Cash, Not Kudos on the same night out [S37]
Note the strip's gangs for Pest Control: the coverage names this district's holders [S14]

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown returns you to the airport from Catch Me If You Can, this time as a full mission with its own trophy [S1][S33]. Do not confuse the two: the missable unscheduled departure belongs to the earlier story visit, while this takedown is a regular completion that can be replayed in order [S9]. Finish it before the finale; its completion is part of the Chapter 4 sweep [S6].
steps: Pick up the VCIA Takedown marker when it appears [S6]
Run the takedown's stages in order and hold the airfield until the objective clears [S33]
Escape or stand down as the mission directs; the trophy pops on completion [S1]
On the way out, register any airfield vehicle you board — airfields hold models the roads never show [S26]
Log the airport layout in your notes; the final heat of bank and truck routes uses the same district [S41]

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is the heaviest of the named missions and the last one before the finale in this guide's staging [S1][S6]. Stock up before you start: it is a long combat mission, and Combat Focus practice here pays off later for Gunslinger's five-takedown window [S13]. Completion is all the trophy asks; performance medals are a different system [S48].
steps: Pick up the Operation Savage Glory marker in the Chapter 4 window [S6]
Restock armour and ammunition before the start — it is the longest named mission [S13]
Complete the operation's stages in order, using Combat Focus on grouped enemies [S13]
Finish the mission; the trophy pops at the completion card [S1]
Count any five-takedown Focus window you managed — that is Gunslinger, rehearsed under fire [S13]
Restock after the operation; the finale assumes a full kit [S19]

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold, and the list's long pole: the game's own 100% statistic, tracked separately from the counted trophies [S1][S2]. The statistic draws on story, strands, activities and collections as a single percentage, so the cheapest route is breadth first — touch every category early, then deepen whatever the in-game checklist still shows as open [S11]. Keep this for last: stages 4 to 6 exist to make the final percentage a short mop-up instead of a second playthrough [S19].
steps: Open the in-game 100% checklist after the story and note every open category [S11]
Clear open story and stranger items first — they close whole categories at once [S28]
Work the counted collections (cards, spots, areas) that the checklist still shows open [S7]
Finish open activities and challenges until the checklist has nothing left [S27]
Push the statistic to 100%; the gold pops when the counter tops out [S1]
If the percentage stalls in the high 90s, compare category by category against the checklist — the gap is always a named item, never a rounding error [S48]
Cross-check the open categories against the guide hub's 100% structure if your own checklist view is unclear [S10]
Expect the last percent to be a collectible class, not a mission — missions close in whole numbers [S7]
When the gold pops, only the platinum remains: check the tracker for the one counter still open [S19]

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: A pure counter silver: 250 completed stunts, tracked as one shared count across both protagonists [S2][S21]. Stunts are the game's marked jump and stunt locations; a stunt only counts when the game registers it as completed, so a crashed landing is practice, not progress [S39]. Route them region by region with the stage-5 sweep and the counter climbs without a dedicated grind until the last few dozen [S25].
steps: Learn what a registered stunt looks like — the game confirms each completed stunt on screen [S39]
Sweep stunt locations region by region alongside the collectibles route [S25]
Split the route between Lucia and Jason freely; the 250 is one shared counter [S21]
Retry failed jumps immediately while the approach is fresh, rather than banking them for later [S39]
At 250 registered stunts the silver pops; the tracker counter should match the game's own count [S2]
If a stunt refuses to register, change vehicle class before changing route — some jumps are tuned for bikes, not cars [S39]
Use the stunt sweep to cross unexplored areas; the stunt map and the 52-area map overlap heavily [S18]
Player statistics make this one of the list's rarer silvers — finishing it early moves you ahead of the field [S46]

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The friendliest trophy on the list: try each of the nine activity types once [S1][S27]. It is cheapest in stage 1, when every unlock is a first by definition; keep a list of the types you have touched and deliberately sample each new one the story introduces [S19]. Variants of a type do not add to the nine — a second race class is still racing [S48].
steps: List the nine activity types from the activity index and tick them as you try each [S27]
Sample every activity the story unlocks in Chapters 1–3 the first time it appears [S27]
Hunt down any untouched type in free roam — fishing, arcade and meditation are the usual stragglers [S38]
Try the ninth type and the trophy pops [S1]

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The hardest silver here: gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, no silvers accepted [S1][S2]. Work range by range and weapon by weapon, learning each challenge's target pattern before chasing the medal score; most players find the last few golds are about one stubborn challenge per range [S39]. Short daily sessions beat one long tilt — accuracy trophies punish tired hands [S16].
steps: Unlock the ranges and post a score in all 42 challenges first, medals aside [S39]
Re-run each challenge to learn its target pattern, then chase gold range by range [S39]
Tackle your worst challenge first in each session, while your aim is fresh [S16]
Track golds in the tracker counter — 42 is the number PSN tracks [S2]
Gold the final challenge and the silver pops [S1]
If one challenge walls you, study its pattern at half pace in the guide coverage before spending attempts [S39]
Keep sessions short and frequent; the platinum reports blame this silver for more stalled runs than any other [S16]

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win — not enter, not place — a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations [S1][S2]. Learn each course with a sighting run, then race it properly; the courses are short and the winning lines are about cutting the marked gates cleanly rather than raw speed [S37]. Because a win is binary, this counter only moves one way: bank the easy coastal courses first [S19].
steps: Find a Top Fun start point and learn the format with one sighting run [S37]
Win at each location in turn; only a win advances the counter [S2]
Re-run a lost course immediately — the gate line is freshest right after a loss [S37]
Bank the open coastal courses before the tight city ones [S19]
Win at the 14th location and the trophy pops [S1]
Mark won locations in the tracker as you go — the game lists entries, not wins, and memory blurs by location nine [S37]
Drone practice doubles as map learning for the northern areas few story missions visit [S18]

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty wins, and the word that matters is "different": the same race won twice counts once [S1]. Spread the wins across race classes and regions — the variety also feeds Master of None's activity sampling and the vehicle discoveries, since race paddocks are dense with new vehicles [S26][S27]. Keep a list of won events in the tracker notes; memory lies at race fourteen [S19].
steps: Win a first race in each class as they unlock, noting each event won [S27]
Work through new events rather than re-running favourites — repeats do not count [S1]
Enter and register paddock vehicles between races for Whip It Good [S26]
Win your 20th distinct race and the trophy pops [S1]
Prefer new events in new districts — each one also crosses an area off The Goodtime State [S18]
If a class frustrates you, bank wins in the classes you enjoy and return with a better vehicle [S37]

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal is one of the named contacts, and his fishing challenge is a one-off contest: beat his catch and the trophy is yours [S1][S28]. It is repeatable, so there is no missable risk — the only mistake is never going [S38]. Learn the fishing timing on ordinary catches first; the challenge is a test of the same mechanic, not a new one [S38].
steps: Meet Cal through the stranger content and unlock his fishing challenge [S28]
Practise ordinary fishing until the catch timing is reliable [S38]
Enter Cal's challenge and land the better catch [S38]
Beat his score and the trophy pops at the result [S1]
Fishing counts toward Master of None's nine activity types — if it is still untried, this trip closes two trophies' work at once [S27]
Cal's spot sits on good hunting water; Bret's strand is the natural next stop in stage 4 [S28]

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game, start to credits, at any cabinet in Leonida [S1]. It takes minutes and unlocks nothing else, which is exactly why it belongs in stage 1: it is the cheapest activity type for Master of None and a free bronze while the story is still young [S27]. Pick the shortest game on the cabinet if several are offered [S19].
steps: Find an arcade cabinet in any Leonida venue [S27]
Start a game and play it to its end — quitting mid-game does not complete it [S1]
Finish the game and the trophy pops [S1]

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's strand ends with a final mission, and finishing the strand is the trophy [S1][S28]. Work his markers in order whenever they appear; strands do not expire as chapters pass, but clearing them in stage 4 keeps the silver strand count tidy [S19]. His strand is one of the eight Strangers & Freaks needs [S28].
steps: Take Andy's first stranger marker when it appears on the map [S28]
Work his strand's missions in order, start to final [S28]
Complete his final mission; the trophy pops on completion [S1]
Count the finished strand toward Strangers & Freaks (8 needed) [S1]
Andy's route crosses two meditation spots — meditate on the same trip (Positive Mental Attitude) [S40]
If his strand is your first, set the pattern: strands in order, finals counted, no half-strands left behind [S19]

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand is the water-flavoured one, and its final mission earns this trophy [S1][S28]. As with Andy, the pattern is simple: take every marker in order and finish the strand [S28]. His missions double as good vehicle-discovery ground — marinas and docks hold boats the road routes never show you [S26].
steps: Take Kenton's first stranger marker when it appears [S28]
Work his strand in order to its final mission [S28]
Register any new boats and vehicles his missions put you in (Whip It Good) [S26]
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops on completion [S1]

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand ends in a final mission, and the trophy is for finishing it [S1][S28]. His is the loneliest route on the map — long rides through the state's quieter counties, which cross several of the 52 areas and are worth combining with the exploration sweep [S18]. Finish the strand and it counts toward the eight Strangers & Freaks needs [S1].
steps: Take Billy's first stranger marker when it appears [S28]
Work his strand in order; note every new area the rides cross (The Goodtime State) [S18]
Complete his final mission; the trophy pops on completion [S1]

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: A silver for breadth: finish any eight stranger strands anywhere in Leonida [S1][S28]. The five named contacts (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five strands with trophies of their own, so this silver is really "the named five plus the three shortest others" [S19]. A strand counts when its final mission is done, not when it is started — half-finished strands are the usual reason this counter stalls at seven [S48].
steps: Finish the five named-contact strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) for their own trophies [S28]
Pick the three shortest remaining strands on the map and finish those [S28]
Count only completed strands — a strand ends at its final mission [S48]
Complete the eighth strand and the silver pops [S1]
Strand order in this guide follows the roadmap's stage 4 exactly — the same order the trophy roadmap recommends [S8]
Leave any ninth strand for the 100% checklist; eight is the whole ask here [S1]

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand is the supply-run one, and finishing his final mission is the trophy [S1][S28]. His routes are delivery driving, which makes them natural partners for vehicle discovery and area exploration on the same trips [S18][S26]. Finish the strand in stage 4 with the other named contacts [S19].
steps: Take Randy's first stranger marker when it appears [S28]
Work his delivery strand in order to its final mission [S28]
Register new vehicles his runs put you in (Whip It Good) [S26]
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops on completion [S1]

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand closes with a final mission, and the trophy follows the same pattern as the other named contacts [S1][S28]. Clear it in stage 4; with his strand done, the named five are complete and Strangers & Freaks needs only three more strands [S19].
steps: Take Tyrone's first stranger marker when it appears [S28]
Work his strand in order to its final mission [S28]
Complete the final mission; the trophy pops on completion [S1]

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida [S1][S2]. The spots sit in the state's scenic corners, so the efficient play is a single routed sweep in stage 5, region by region, alongside the other counted collectibles [S40]. Neither source adds a time-of-day condition, whatever the sunrise rumour says [S48]. Two spots sit near the Child's Play mission area and can be taken during the story [S40].
steps: Mark the 18 meditation spots region by region before you set out [S40]
Meditate at each spot until the game registers the visit [S1]
Take the two spots near the Child's Play area during the story to shorten the sweep [S40]
Keep the tracker counter matched to the game's count — 18 is PSN's target [S2]
Meditate at the 18th spot and the trophy pops [S1]
The spots make natural rest points in the area sweep — pair each with its region's cards and WAiNK spots [S23]
Photograph nothing and rush nothing: the spots are the sweep's scenic spine, and the map threads name them among Leonida's best views [S15]

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret wants one unique animal hunted, and the trophy is for delivering that hunt [S1][S28]. Unique means a specific marked animal, not any member of the species: work Bret's strand until the hunt itself is offered, then track the marked animal rather than the first one you see [S44]. It is the trickiest of the stage-4 bronzes, so bring the best hunting vehicle and daylight [S19].
steps: Take Bret's stranger marker and work his strand to the hunt [S28]
Wait for the unique animal to be marked — ordinary animals of the species do not count [S44]
Track and hunt the marked animal, then report back to Bret [S44]
Complete the hunt and the trophy pops [S1]
Warm up on ordinary game in the same country so the tracking controls are second nature before the unique animal [S44]
Bret's country borders two unexplored areas for most players — cross them on the way home [S18]

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: A silver for finishing any three complete collectible card sets — the description names no set, so the choice is yours [S1][S2]. Pick the three sets whose cards cluster along the story and sweep routes; a set is only done when every card in it is collected, so track per-card, not per-set, in your notes [S25]. Cards are the densest collectible on the map and the usual last item in a region sweep [S23].
steps: Choose the three sets whose cards sit closest to your existing routes [S25]
Collect every card of the first set, tracking each card individually [S23]
Complete the second and third sets the same way [S25]
Finish the last card of the third set and the silver pops [S1]
Work from the collectible maps when a set stalls at one card — the last card is always a place, never a random drop [S24]
Leftover cards beyond three sets still feed the 100% checklist, so nothing collected is wasted [S7]

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 different locations — the count is of places, not uses, so a spot counts once [S1][S2]. WAiNK spots cluster in the built-up districts, especially around the nightlife strip you visit for Headliners, and the sweep is best done district by district in stage 5 [S23]. Keep the counter honest: if the game does not register the spot, it did not happen [S19].
steps: Find a first WAiNK spot and learn the interaction the game wants [S23]
Sweep the nightlife and downtown districts, where spots cluster [S23]
Move district by district, counting only spots the game registers [S2]
WAiNK It at the 100th distinct location and the silver pops [S1]
The community megathreads keep a running district tally — sanity-check your count against the districts, not your memory [S15]
Finish this inside stage 5: WAiNK spots thin out outside the built-up districts, so a late start means a city-only grind [S23]

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Fifty completions from the game's own challenge list, tracked by PSN to 50 [S1][S2][S42]. Challenges are the short repeatable tasks scattered through Leonida's systems; the fast route is to clear the short ones in every category first and leave the long performance challenges for stage 6 sessions [S19]. Story missions are not challenges — they have their own trophies [S48].
steps: Open the challenge list and sort by your shortest completions first [S42]
Clear the quick challenges in every category to build the count cheaply [S42]
Work the longer performance challenges in stage 6 sessions [S19]
Complete the 50th challenge and the trophy pops [S1]
Challenges refresh the route: alternate a challenge with a collectible leg so stage 6 never becomes one long list [S19]
Any challenge tied to a place the Newswire tours is worth doing early, while its district is already on your route [S4]

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, and get clear [S1]. "Partner" is the other protagonist — the game's partner system, not a second player [S30][S45]. The reliable shape: raise exactly four stars somewhere with a fast car and a hiding route, keep your partner in the car, and break line of sight until the stars drain [S34]. Going past four stars works too, but four is the floor the description names [S1].
steps: Pick a spot with a fast car, your partner present, and a covered escape route [S34]
Commit crimes in the open until the wanted level reaches four stars [S1]
Keep your partner with you — do not swap away or leave them behind [S30]
Break line of sight and hide until the wanted level is fully lost [S34]
Escape the area clean and the trophy pops [S1]
Rehearse the escape at three stars first if four-star heat keeps ending in a bust — the shape is identical, the margin bigger [S34]
The session notes agree this is the easier of the two partner trophies; take it before Retail Therapy [S45]

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Three shop robberies back-to-back, partner present, and the wanted level must never be lost in between — fully cleared, busted or wasted all break the chain [S1][S48]. Choose three shops on one straight road so the drive between them keeps the heat simmering without a chase spiral [S34]. This is the fiddliest of the partner trophies; do it with a fast car and full health [S19].
steps: Pick three shops on one straight route and park a fast car outside the first [S34]
Rob the first shop with your partner present and take the wanted level it gives [S1]
Drive straight to the second shop, keeping the wanted level alive — never let it fully clear [S48]
Rob the second, then the third, the same way [S34]
Escape after the third robbery and the trophy pops [S1]
If the chain breaks at shop two, restart the chain rather than improvising — the counter needs three in a row, not three in a day [S48]
Keep the partner's health up between shops; a downed partner ends the run as surely as a bust [S30]

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle counts when you get in and the game registers it, not when you merely see it [S26]. Leonida's traffic variety does most of the work: ports, marinas, the airport and rich districts each hold models the highways never show [S26]. Marry this to the Scooter Bros registrations: every new vehicle you enter is a registration candidate too [S36].
steps: Get into every unfamiliar vehicle you pass in the early game — the first 50 come free [S26]
Work the specialist grounds: marina boats, airport vehicles, port machinery [S26]
Register each new vehicle to Scooter Bros as you discover it (On the Spot) [S36]
Enter your 100th distinct vehicle and the trophy pops [S1]
The official site's vehicle-flavoured showcases hint at where the exotic models live — rich districts and the Keys [S29]
Player statistics put this among the most-earned bronzes; if your count lags, you are skipping a vehicle class, usually boats [S46]

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Five takedowns inside one Combat Focus window [S1]. The trick is staging, not aim: gather a group of five or more enemies in the open — a gang operation or a botched robbery works — line them up, then trigger Focus once and work left to right [S13]. Operation Savage Glory's set-pieces are a natural practice ground [S13]. Knockdowns count; the description says take down, not kill [S48].
steps: Find or provoke a group of at least five enemies in the open [S13]
Position so all five are visible without turning far [S13]
Trigger Combat Focus once and take down all five inside the window [S1]
If the window ends at four, re-stage with a bigger group rather than a faster trigger finger [S19]

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.ponr: Point of no return: the VCIA story visit in the Chapter 3 window. Once that mission resolves, the unscheduled departure cannot be replayed on this save — take it during the visit.
trophies.guide: The list's clearest missable: during the story's VCIA visit, leave the airport in an unscheduled way — not the exit the mission lays out for you [S1][S33]. The description's joke is the instruction: a departure nobody scheduled. This guide flags it because the moment belongs to one story beat and the save cannot rewind to it [S9]. If you are reading this before Chapter 3, you are in time; keep a save at the chapter start as insurance [S19].
steps: Keep a manual save at the start of Chapter 3, before the VCIA visit [S9]
Play the VCIA story visit until you are free to move inside the airport [S33]
Instead of the mission's marked exit, take an unscheduled way out — an unplanned vehicle or an unmarked route off the field [S22]
Clear the airport boundary and the trophy pops [S1]
If the mission resolves first, reload the chapter-start save — after the finale this window is gone [S19]
Scout the airfield's unmarked exits on arrival, before the mission's markers start pulling you [S33]
This is the missable the solution notes warn about most — if you only insure one trophy with a save, insure this one [S22]

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: "In these Rhinos" puts you inside the tank, so the trophy is about taking a Rhino and using it, not fighting one [S1][S48]. Rhinos appear where the military answers high wanted levels and around the state's heavy installations; the clean route is to draw one out, clear its crew, and climb in [S22]. Once you are in, make it count — a short rampage is the spirit of the thing [S22].
steps: Raise a high wanted level near a military response route, or watch the heavy installations [S22]
When a Rhino arrives, clear its crew and take the driver's seat [S22]
Use the Rhino — drive it and fire the cannon — until the game registers the deed [S1]
The trophy pops once the Rhino run is registered [S1]

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store clean: in, emptied, out, and never detected [S1]. Detection is the fail state, not the alarm after you leave — case the store first, note the staff and camera positions, and go at a quiet hour with a covered face and a parked escape car [S34]. If you are spotted, walk away and reset rather than forcing it; a blown attempt teaches the layout for free [S19].
steps: Case a jewelry store: staff positions, cameras, the quietest hour [S34]
Enter covered, control the room quietly, and empty the cases [S34]
Leave by your planned route before any detection registers [S1]
Clear the area undetected and the trophy pops [S1]

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: A silver for robbing five bank vaults and escaping each time [S1][S41]. Treat each bank as its own job — this guide routes five different banks rather than repeating one — and reuse the Cartel Heist rhythm: vault, timer, escape route, lose the heat [S41]. An escape only counts when the wanted level is fully lost after the robbery [S34].
steps: Learn the vault routine on the first bank: entry, vault timer, exit route [S41]
Rob the vault and escape until the wanted level is fully lost [S34]
Move to a different bank for each of the five — variety keeps the routes honest [S19]
Rob the fifth vault and escape; the silver pops [S1]
Vary your escape vehicle class between banks — the response adapts to a repeated pattern [S41]
Bank robbery income is clean money; the laundering counter only tracks marked bills, so do not confuse the two ledgers [S42]

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: One armored truck, robbed and escaped from [S1][S41]. The trucks run predictable bank routes; the working method is to stop the truck somewhere with a clean exit, crack the rear doors, take the cash and be gone before the response builds [S41]. It is a single deed, not a counter — one clean truck is the whole trophy [S1].
steps: Learn an armored truck's route from a bank and pick a quiet stop point with an exit [S41]
Stop the truck and open the rear doors [S41]
Take the cash and leave immediately — do not fight the response at the truck [S34]
Lose the wanted level fully; the trophy pops on the escape [S1]

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — an area registers when you enter its heartland and its name shows, not when you clip its border road [S2][S18]. The sweep is the spine of stage 5: route it region by region and the collectibles, stunts and spots along the way advance with it [S19]. The last areas are always the far corners — the Keys and the northern counties [S18].
steps: Open the map and divide Leonida into regions for the sweep [S18]
Enter each area's heartland until its name registers [S18]
Fold the region's collectibles and stunts into the same pass [S19]
Explore the 52nd area and the trophy pops [S1]
The PlayStation Blog's Leonida features name the headline regions — use them as your sweep checklist's skeleton [S5]
Areas left dark after the sweep are listed by the map threads in the same order this guide routes them [S15]

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation for each of Leonida's nine gangs — it is one per gang, not any nine operations [S1][S33]. Identify operations by the gang that holds them before you go in; the tracker lists this counter by gang so a repeat on the same gang never masquerades as progress [S19]. Each robbery is its own small heist: case it, hit it, escape [S34].
steps: List the nine gangs and one reachable operation for each [S33]
Rob the first gang's operation and escape clean [S34]
Work through the remaining gangs, one operation each [S33]
Rob the ninth gang's operation and the trophy pops [S1]
The region coverage names which gang holds which coast — plan the nine as a coastal circuit, not a scatter [S14]
Operations respawn for money, but the trophy needs only the first robbery per gang [S33]

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.ponr: Point of no return: the game's opening stretch on Ocean Beach. Have the cocktail during your first Ocean Beach visit in Chapter 1 — the moment belongs to the beginning, and this guide does not trust it to wait.
trophies.guide: A two-minute trophy with a long shadow: enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach [S1][S43]. The title — "In The Beginning…" — and the opening framing are why this guide flags it missable: the moment belongs to the start of the game, and the safe play is to take it on your first Ocean Beach visit in Chapter 1 [S19]. It costs almost nothing and forgetting it can cost a replay [S9].
steps: On your first Ocean Beach visit in Chapter 1, find the cocktail spot with the view [S43]
Order and enjoy the cocktail; let the moment play out [S1]
The trophy pops as the moment completes [S1]
If you are past Chapter 1 without it, check the spot anyway — but do not plan a platinum route that relies on it waiting [S19]
Ocean Beach is the Newswire's postcard shot of Vice City — the cocktail spot faces that same view [S4]
Take a breath here: this is the last quiet trophy before the missable windows start stacking in Chapter 2 [S9]

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle out through a showroom's glass, in the series' classic style [S1][S43]. Neither list names a specific showroom or car, so any vehicle showroom qualifies in this guide's reading: get in a car inside, line up the window, and go through it rather than the door [S22]. It is a thirty-second trophy once you are standing in the showroom [S19].
steps: Enter any vehicle showroom and get into a car on the floor [S43]
Line the car up with the showroom window, not the door [S22]
Accelerate through the glass and out onto the street [S1]
The trophy pops as you clear the showroom [S1]

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play the bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley and follow through — the description's joke is a bowling term, and the trophy is for playing the game there [S1]. It is not the same trophy as Ten Pin, which is a drive-by stunt that merely shares the bowling vocabulary [S48]. One visit, one game, one bronze [S19]. Note the official name uses a curly apostrophe, as PlayStation publishes it [S3].
steps: Travel to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley [S1]
Start a bowling game at the alley [S27]
Play the game through with a proper follow-through on your throws [S1]
Finish the game and the trophy pops [S1]

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.ponr: Point of no return: the partnership story beat in the Chapter 2–3 window. It plays once, inside the story; finish the chapter with it taken, or reload the chapter-start save.
trophies.guide: The vaguest description on the list — "A partnership with mass appeal" — and a hidden trophy among the story beats, which is why this guide flags it missable [S1][S9]. Nothing in either source ties it to an ending or a choice; it belongs to a partnership moment in the Chapter 2–3 window, where Lucia and Jason's double act takes centre stage [S19][S31]. Keep the chapter-start save until it pops [S19].
steps: Keep a manual save at the start of Chapter 2 [S9]
Play the Chapter 2–3 story beats with both protagonists together — do not split them for side content in this window [S31]
Take the partnership moment when the story offers it, in full, without skipping [S1]
The trophy pops as the beat completes; if the chapter ends without it, reload the chapter-start save [S19]
The cover story's account of the partner system is the best primer for why this beat matters to the pair [S31]
Do the chapter's side content after the beat, not before — the window is the chapter itself [S19]

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.ponr: Point of no return: each story choice itself. A branch not taken cannot be re-chosen on the same save, so make every prompted choice as it comes rather than letting scenes lapse.
trophies.guide: PSN tracks this one to 500 choices, which settles the old argument about what counts: ordinary prompted choices, made one by one through the game [S2]. Most of the 500 come free by playing attentively; the missable risk is only in letting story choices lapse or skipping branches, since a choice not made cannot be re-chosen on the same save [S21]. There is no right answer to pick — the trophy counts choosing, not choosing well [S1].
steps: Make every prompted choice as it appears — never let a choice timer lapse [S2]
Take optional conversations and branch points instead of walking past them [S21]
Watch the tracker counter climb with the story; it should pass 500 before the finale if you engage with everything [S2]
Make the 500th tracked choice and the trophy pops [S1]
If the counter lags the story, the missing choices are optional conversations — the forum ruling is that they count like any other [S21]
Alternate protagonists' scenes where the game lets you: both halves of the pair generate choices [S31]

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.ponr: Point of no return: the scripted first attempt inside the final-mission sequence. Do not reload when the first attempt falls short — play through the shortfall, or the second attempt never happens.
trophies.guide: "Second time's the charm" is a scripted beat, not a farming instruction: somewhere in the endgame a first attempt is built to fall short, and the trophy is for succeeding on the second [S1][S22]. The trap is reloading when the first attempt fails — that erases the sequence. Flagged missable for exactly that reason: play through the failure [S19].
steps: Play the endgame sequence without reloading at the scripted shortfall [S22]
Let the first attempt fail as written — it is meant to [S22]
Take the second attempt the story offers and succeed [S1]
The trophy pops on the second-attempt success [S1]

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.ponr: Point of no return: the stranger-strand encounter that triggers it. Work the strands in stage 4 without rushing past odd encounters — once the strand closes, the moment does not repeat on this save.
trophies.guide: The list's UFO-flavoured secret: witness something strange [S1]. It sits hidden among the stranger content in the list's ordering, so this guide routes it through the stage-4 strands and flags it missable: when a strand encounter turns weird, stay and watch it play out instead of driving away [S28]. No source pins the trigger to a random event, and this guide does not invent one — it tells you where the strangeness lives: inside the stranger strands [S48].
steps: Work the stranger strands in stage 4 in order [S28]
When an encounter turns strange, stay for the whole event — do not leave mid-scene [S28]
Witness the event to its end; the trophy pops as it concludes [S1]
If a strand closes with nothing strange seen, note it in the tracker — the moment is strand-bound and does not repeat [S19]
The places threads swap theories about this one endlessly; trust the list's ordering over the theories [S15]
Night visits to strand country are the community's one consistent tip — atmosphere, at least, is guaranteed [S43]

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A stunt in bowling clothes: knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle — a melee drive-by [S1]. It is not earned at the bowling alley; that is Let's Go Bowling, a different trophy sharing the vocabulary [S48]. Any cluster of pedestrians and a slow pass with the melee button out does it [S19].
steps: Find a group of pedestrians on a quiet street [S19]
Drive past slowly and use the melee attack from the vehicle as you pass [S1]
Knock a pedestrian down with the drive-by melee; the trophy pops [S1]

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts — a specific pipeline, not general income, so story payouts and robbery cash do not advance it [S1][S2]. Marked bills come from the jobs that pay in them; bank them through the laundering contacts as they accumulate rather than spending them, and the counter is a steady stage-6 companion to the robbery trophies [S42]. PSN tracks the full $250,000 [S2].
steps: Unlock the laundering contacts through the story and Randy's supply world [S28]
Take jobs that pay in Marked Bills and keep the bills for laundering [S42]
Launder in batches through your contacts; only laundered money advances the counter [S1]
Reach $250,000 laundered and the trophy pops [S1]
Alternate laundering batches with bank vaults so both money-adjacent counters climb in the same stage [S41]
Keep a laundering reserve: spending marked bills raw is the one way to make this counter slower [S42]

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in shops — shops, specifically: the garage properties have their own trophy and their own budget [S1][S35]. Ordinary play gets much of this (weapons, clothes, vehicles services, food), and the tail is cheapest at the end of stage 6 when cash is plentiful [S19]. Keep the two money trophies separate in your head: laundering is Dime on the Dollar, spending is this one [S48].
steps: Spend normally through the game — weapons, clothing, services all count [S35]
Check the counter late in stage 6 and note the shortfall [S2]
Top up with deliberate shopping — outfits and vehicle work are the fastest sinks [S35]
Pass $100,000 spent in shops and the trophy pops [S1]
Outfits for both protagonists are the pleasantest sink — the official site's character pages are a wardrobe catalogue [S29]
Do not sell-and-rebuy to farm this: only spending counts, and the tracker follows PSN's figure [S2]

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all eight garage properties on the map [S1][S2]. Neither source locks any of them behind the story, but the prices argue for buying late, when the robbery and laundering income of stage 6 is flowing — this guide stages the purchases in stage 5 and pays for them in stage 6 if cash is tight [S19][S35]. Each purchase registers immediately; there is no set bonus to chase beyond the eighth [S48].
steps: List the eight garage properties on the map as you explore (The Goodtime State) [S18]
Buy garages as cash allows, cheapest first [S35]
Keep story and robbery income flowing until all eight are affordable [S19]
Buy the eighth garage and the trophy pops [S1]
Garages double as the sweep's fast-travel anchors — buy the far-corner ones first [S19]
A full garage row is also the natural home for the registered Scooter Bros fleet [S36]

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — an app action on vehicles you drive, owned or not [S1][S36]. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good: every new vehicle you enter to discover it can be registered on the spot, so the two counters finish within minutes of each other if you work them together [S19]. Ten is a small number; most players complete it accidentally in the sweep [S36].
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app in-game and learn the registration action [S36]
Register each new vehicle as you enter it for Whip It Good [S36]
Register the tenth vehicle and the trophy pops [S1]
Register story-given vehicles first — they are the ten you are most likely to keep [S36]
Registration is permanent per vehicle, so there is no way to lose progress on this one [S48]
